title: judgekeeper records, version 2
description: One judged answer per JSON line: a judge's verdict (annotator_kind LLM), a person's label (HUMAN) or a code check (CODE). Field names follow OpenInference annotations. Only a verdict is needed in practice (label or score); every field is optional. Fields not listed here are allowed and kept. A record without schema_version is version 1, which has the same fields minus metadata, rule, trajectory, outcome and app_version.

schema_version.description: The records format version. Missing means 1. This schema is version 2.

target_id.description: The answer's id. Missing: derived from input and output (and the trajectory, when there is one).

name.description: Which judge, metric or criterion. Default: judge.

annotator_kind.description: LLM (a judge's verdict, the default), HUMAN (a person's label) or CODE (a code check, left out). Any case; LLM_JUDGE, JUDGE, HUMAN_ANNOTATION and HEURISTIC are read as those.

label.description: The verdict: pass or fail, true or false, a bool, or a value --label-map maps.

score.description: A number. Read as the verdict with --pass-if, or when label is empty.

run.description: Which repeat this verdict is from. Empty: each file is one run.

input.description: The question or input, as text or any JSON.

output.description: The answer that was judged, as text or any JSON.

evaluator.description: The judge's identity. A string must hold this object as JSON (as a CSV cell does).

created_at.description: When the verdict was made, ISO 8601.

metadata.description: Anything else: a criterion name, a run id, an A/B version. Kept and passed on; never part of the judge's identity.

trajectory.description: The agent's steps that led to the output, as OpenAI-style messages. Kept in the anchor set; not shown on any page yet.

outcome.description: An automatic check of the result (unit tests, a database check).

app_version.description: The version of the app or agent that produced the output. judgekeeper start says when it changes between checks.

provider.description: Who serves the judge's model, e.g. anthropic, openai.

prompt.description: The judge's prompt; judgekeeper keeps only its hash.

prompt_hash.description: sha256 of the prompt, when the prompt itself is not given.

snapshot.description: The model snapshot the provider served.

endpoint.description: The endpoint the judge was called at; null means the provider's default.

rule.description: The judge's rule in words (GEval criteria and steps, an llm-rubric value). Hashed into the prompt hash when there is no prompt or prompt_hash.

content.description: Text, a list of content parts, or null (an assistant step that only calls tools).

tool_call_id.description: On a tool step: the id of the call it answers.

arguments.description: The arguments, as an object or as JSON text.

source.description: What checked it, e.g. unit tests, database check, SWE-bench resolved.
